Death could mean hell for you, or not. Or it could be nothingness. Or it could be worse than any hell captured in any religious scripture or personal imagination. Ah, yeahhhh, then it could also be paradise, I suppose. Or another life.

Endless possibilities aside, the only thing we know for sure is that death is completely unknown. I personally applied the Pascal's Wager thing and assumed death could easily be infinitely worse than life. Not only that, but I acknowledged that I may have zero (NO and NONEXISTENT) control over that afterlife. As dark and difficult as this life becomes, I have to admit, there is still so much I can control and change.

So, for me, the possibility of death being worse than life was not anti-motivating by itself. When I consider the amount of control I may lose after death, though.... That is frightening.
My apologies for the not-fun-Friday material, but: If you've ever considered suicide, what are your thoughts on death being worse than whatever hell you are enduring in this life?
The moments before death will last more than a lifetime if one is full of regret. Time is ephemeral. It's not about the afterlife, in my opinion, and more about getting there. Live life: No ragrets

My way of thinking is if I can't figure out how to enjoy myself here and now, what makes me think I'll have any better luck in the next life? Better to try a little harder now, besides this life doesn't last forever. We all die, might as well embrace living until it's over.

I wonder what's next.

Also you only ever have exactly this moment. Given that, any thoughts of death are just that : thoughts. Better stated, abstractions. Thinking about the future or the past is illusory because they don't exist. Now is it. When your dead it will also be now.

In summary, let's hope it's better than this life.
